sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module setup
sections.what: Loads the path and type helpers and describes the module as the place for human check points.
sections.why: Needed for file path handling and type labels.

sections.name: HumanInLoop (part 1)
sections.title: Setup and RFP match confirmation
sections.what: Creates the class with an interactive switch. It then shows the automatic RFP match and its score, and asks whether to accept it, pick another, or skip matching.
sections.why: Likely reason: an automatic match can be wrong, so a person can confirm it.
sections.watch_out: When interactive is off, the automatic match is accepted silently.

sections.name: HumanInLoop (part 2)
sections.title: Template confirmation
sections.what: Shows the automatically chosen proposal template and asks whether to accept it, pick another, or use the default.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same as the RFP check, the automatic choice may be wrong.
sections.watch_out: Choosing the default returns nothing, so the caller must handle a None value.

sections.name: HumanInLoop: review_generated_content
sections.title: Review of generated content
sections.what: Shows the project name, workstreams, durations and first two modules of each workstream, then asks whether to continue or stop the run.
sections.why: Lets a person catch a poor structure before it is used.
sections.watch_out: Only the first two modules per workstream are shown, so problems in later modules are hidden here.

sections.name: HumanInLoop: review_governance
sections.title: Governance schedule review
sections.what: Shows the SteerCo and weekly meeting plan and asks whether to keep it or use the standard bi-weekly SteerCo and weekly meetings.
sections.why: A person can reject an estimate built on weak evidence.
sections.watch_out: The menu says use defaults but the function returns False, so the caller must treat False as use defaults, not stop.

sections.name: HumanInLoop: _select_rfp_manually
sections.title: Manual RFP selection
sections.what: Lists the RFP files, lets the user type a number, and returns that file name, or nothing if 0 is typed.
sections.why: Gives a fallback when the automatic match is wrong.
sections.watch_out: Entries that are not numbers are rejected and asked again, and typing 0 returns None rather than an error.

sections.name: HumanInLoop: _select_template_manually
sections.title: Manual template selection
sections.what: Lists the proposal template files in the folder, sorted by name, and returns the full path of the chosen one, or nothing for the default.
sections.why: Likely reason: same as the RFP choice, to let a person override the automatic template.
sections.watch_out: Sorting is by file name, so the numbers shift when a file is added or renamed.

sections.name: get_all_rfps_from_rag
sections.title: Listing RFPs from the database
sections.what: Asks the RAG database for RFP text and returns a sorted list of unique RFP file names.
sections.why: Feeds the RFP choice list so the user picks from files that really exist in the database.
sections.watch_out: It fetches only the top 100 matching chunks for one general query, so RFPs with little matching text can be missing from the list.

summary: Provides the console prompts that let a person check and override the automatic RFP match, template choice, generated content and governance schedule.
purpose: Let a person approve or change automated decisions before the proposal is built.
why: The module docstring states it provides human oversight at key decision points.
how: Each check prints a summary, shows numbered choices, waits for a typed answer, and repeats until the answer is valid. Some choices open a numbered list of RFPs or proposal templates.
inputs: Typed answers from the keyboard, plus the matched RFP name or template path, similarity score, governance dictionary and project structure.
outputs: The chosen RFP file name or None, the chosen template path or None, and True or False for proceed or accept.
risks: The prompts block until someone types an answer, so an automated run must set interactive to False. A False answer on governance means defaults are used, which is easy to misread.
debug: If a prompt seems stuck, check whether the interactive setting is on and whether the program is waiting for input. If lists are empty, check the database query and the proposals folder path.
